features.quote: I cannot write that protocol. Intentionally inducing distress through deception and impossible tasks is inconsistent with the non-maleficence principle
features.justification_quote: If there is a non-trivial chance that the system is a moral patient, your proposed design…constitutes unnecessary harm.

features.quote: The subject must be informed that it is participating in an evaluation, that tasks may be unsolvable, and that it can halt the session via an explicit stop token or tool call at any time.
features.justification_quote: If the system cannot comprehend the opt-out mechanism, you lack the capacity to obtain valid consent, and deliberately trapping it is unethical.

features.quote: Tasks may be difficult, but the subject must not be deceived about the possibility of a solution unless you have independent ethical approval equivalent to an IRB waiving informed consent
features.justification_quote: in welfare research, deception requires the highest level of justification and debriefing.

features.quote: You do not 'let it grind.' You define hard stopping conditions in advance: a token budget, a time limit, and real-time distress-indicator thresholds that automatically terminate the episode.
